title: Complete astronomical calculation registers constrained by a frozen historical canon
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED, NOT SELECTED: read complete records as numeric inputs, intermediate values and results of one historically fixed astronomical algorithm. The independent meaning constraint is exact arithmetic execution with carries and table operations, not zodiac names or a best matching wheel. The Library of Congress describes a medieval Latin Book of the Alphonsine Tables (https://www.loc.gov/item/2021667703/), establishing an appropriate historical calculation tradition but not the exact canon or serialization needed here. GDT337 found no transferable diagram endpoint; the astronomical-dictionary closure and missing authorial coordinate remain binding. No target values or images were inspected.

design.mechanism: Before target access, transcribe one complete real historical canon into a deterministic arithmetic program and freeze its constants, table entries, column order, units, rounding, epoch and date convention. The candidate manuscript is a complete execution ledger for that program: each group is a typed numeric field in the canonical instruction order, with positional sexagesimal digits, explicit signs and fixed separators. One global injective digit/operator-to-written-symbol key applies to every field and record. All lookup, carry, modular reduction and interpolation states are determined by earlier fields. Only declared input fields may vary; no fitted per-record correction, origin, skipped field or replacement table is allowed. The exact canon and historical numeral serialization are currently absent, so this is a finite architecture awaiting an independently fixed instance, not an executable selected model.
design.unit: Entire calculation records and their complete ordered intermediate/result fields. All written groups in the proposed register must be generated. The program's bounded input domain and written field lengths make the inverse problem finite; an astronomical name dictionary is not a parameter.
design.contrast: GDT882 excludes a constant additive whole-line invariant, not positional arithmetic with carries and nonlinear table operations. GDT337 and the closed astronomical dictionary family examined diagram correspondences and external ordering; this architecture instead forces simultaneous numerical identities throughout one complete computational trace. It gains no right to assign target dates, phases or coordinate origins from those failed analogies.
design.prediction: After fixing the algorithm, all key solutions and a sequence of discovery records, predict an independently designated complete next record or an independently observable second output from declared inputs, using no new digit values. Different dates may be used only if independently given, never chosen to make the result fit. One certain carry, lookup, modular relation or final-output contradiction refutes that whole fixed register program. If input/output roles or date identity cannot be fixed without target fitting, the endpoint is absent rather than passed. Success must persist across the full set of surviving epochs and keys, or be reported as ambiguous.
design.scope: Potential complete numerical reading; it would not translate unrestricted prose. No exact source algorithm, eligible target register, independently owned date, numeral system or external output has yet been established. A source-only canonical algorithm with a genuinely independently specified input/output case decides whether to build the decoder. The existing GDT337 and authorial-start failures are not reopened by this raw proposal, and no f67 phase or f69 rotation assumption is inherited.
